defs.def: a part of a tree that grows out from the main stem and on which leaves, flowers and fruit grow 树枝

ex.s: Grabbing a branch from a cut-down tree, he jumped in through the window.
ex.t: 他从一棵砍倒的树上折下一根树枝，从窗户跳了进去。

ex.s: Amazingly, the trees grow in such a way that their leaves and branches, although close together, never actually touch those of another tree.
ex.t: 令人惊奇的是，这些树的生长方式使得它们的叶子和树枝虽然靠得很近，却从不真正触碰到另一棵树的叶子和树枝。

ex.s: Once the book you've requested is delivered to the nearest branch, they will inform you by e-mail, so you can pick it up.
ex.t: 一旦你借的书送到最近的分馆，他们会通过电子邮件通知你，这样你就可以去取了。

ex.s: giving access to online reading at a library branch
ex.t: 在图书馆分馆提供在线阅读权限

ex.s: sending a needed book to a library branch nearby
ex.t: 把需要的书送到附近的图书馆分馆

ex.s: Hospital patients Who see tree branches out their window are likely to recover at a faster rate than patients who see buildings or sky instead.
ex.src: 2019全国I卷·Is Fresh Air Really Good for You?
ex.t: 从窗户能看到树枝的医院病人，康复速度可能比看建筑和天空的病人更快。

ex.s: I put some pine branches into the basket to make this nest safe and comfortable.
ex.t: 我在篮子里放了一些松枝，让这个巢既安全又舒适。

ex.s: And while many Brits like nothing better than spending their Sunday cutting the grass, some are happy just to sit under the branches of the trees and enjoy the beauty of the world around them.
ex.t: 虽然许多英国人最喜欢的事情莫过于在周日修剪草坪，但有些人也乐于坐在树枝下，享受周围世界的美丽。

ex.s: Without enough food to go around, and under pressure from the new arrivals, the green lizards moved higher up the trees, where it is harder to keep a grip on the smoother branches.
ex.t: 在食物不足、又受新来者压力的情况下，绿色蜥蜴移到了树上更高的地方，那里更难在更光滑的枝条上抓稳。

ex.s: The little plum tree outside, with the faintly flushed snow lining its branches and artfully disposed along its trunk, stood in full sunlight.
ex.t: 窗外那棵小李子树，枝条上淡淡地衬着浅红的积雪，精心点缀着树干，傲然挺立在灿烂的阳光下。

ex.s: Like other deer, they lived together and ate grass as well as the soft parts of trees, such as small branches.
ex.t: 像其他鹿一样，它们群居，吃草以及树木柔软的部分，比如小树枝。

ex.s: You must leave right now!” he called out, holding the branch with both hands.
ex.t: “你必须现在就离开！”他双手抓着树枝喊道。

defs.def: a local office or shop/store belonging to a large company or organization 分支；分部；分行；分店

ex.s: Head Chef David Thompson, who received a Michelin star for his Loodon-based Thai restaurant of the same name, opened this branch in the Metropolitan Hotel in 2010.
ex.t: 主厨大卫·汤普森曾凭借其位于伦敦的同名泰国餐厅获得米其林一星，他于2010年在大都会酒店开设了这家分店。

defs.def: a part of a government or other large organization that deals with one particular aspect of its work 政府部门；分支机构

ex.s: Maybe the first plant just made a cry of pain or was sending a message to its own branches, and so, in effect, was talking to itself.
ex.t: 也许第一株植物只是发出了一声痛苦的呐喊，或者是在向自己的枝干传递信息，因此实际上是在跟自己说话。

defs.def: a division of an area of knowledge or a group of languages （学科及语言的）分支

ex.s: This requires commitment to a particular occupation, branch of study or research.
ex.t: 这需要对某一特定职业、学科或研究领域的投入。

defs.def: a smaller or less important part of a river, road, railway/railroad, etc. that leads away from the main part 支流；支路；支线
a group of members of a family who all have the same ancestors 家族分支

ex.s: We have picnics, read books under big trees, and listen to the birds singing in the branches.
ex.t: 我们野餐、在大树下读书，听鸟儿在枝头歌唱。

defs.def: to be joined to another road or river but lead in a different direction 路或河

ex.s: Why do the leaves and branches of different trees avoid touching each other?
ex.t: 为什么不同树木的枝叶会避免相互接触？

defs.def: to leave a road or path and travel in a different direction 人
